card.title: Kinetic theory — pressure from molecular bombardment

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: A gas is a swarm of tiny elastic billiard balls in random motion; pressure is just their collective hammering on the walls, and temperature is their average translational kinetic energy per molecule (½m·c²-bar = 3kT/2). The ideal gas equation PV = nRT is the macroscopic shadow of this microscopic storm. RMS speed ranks molecular speeds by energy, not by average.

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: PV = nRT = NkT (R = 8.31 J/mol·K, k = 1.38×10⁻²³ J/K)  ·  P = (1/3)ρc²-bar  ·  average KE per molecule = 3kT/2 (∝ T only!)  ·  c_rms = √(3RT/M)  ·  O₂ at 27 °C (300 K): c_rms = √(3×8.31×300/0.032) ≈ 484 m/s

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Ideal behaviour needs point molecules, perfectly elastic collisions, no intermolecular forces, and negligible molecular volume — real gases oblige only at low pressure and high temperature. The model assumes a huge number of molecules so averages are sharp, and random isotropic motion (no bulk flow).

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Average KE depends on T alone — same T, same molecular energy for every gas; RMS speed then sorts by mass (lighter = faster: H₂ outruns O₂). O₂ at 27 °C: c_rms ≈ 484 m/s (NEB 2022). Heat capacities split: Cp − Cv = R, with γ = Cp/Cv ≈ 1.4 (diatomic), 1.67 (monoatomic).

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: RMS speed of O₂ at 27 °C = 300 K, M = 0.032 kg/mol: c_rms = √(3RT/M) = √(3 × 8.31 × 300 / 0.032) = √(2.34×10⁵) ≈ 484 m/s (NEB 2022, 3 marks). Same formula with M = 0.002 gives H₂ ≈ 1930 m/s — the reason hydrogen escapes atmospheres.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Real gases deviate at high P (finite molecular volume) and low T (attractions matter) — van der Waals corrects both. The model ignores vibrations/rotations at room T (heat-capacity shortfalls) and quantum effects for light gases at cryogenic T. RMS ≠ mean ≠ most probable speed.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: One molecule bouncing between walls distance L: momentum kick 2mvₓ per hit, hit rate vₓ/2L → force mvₓ²/L. Summing N molecules and averaging over isotropy (vₓ²-bar = c²-bar/3) over area L² gives P = (1/3)ρc²-bar; with ρ = Nm/V, PV = (2/3)N(½mc²-bar) = NkT, identifying temperature with molecular energy.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: 'State assumptions' is the 5-marker (NEB 2023 asked exactly this) — memorise: large N, point mass, elastic collisions, no forces, random motion. RMS: always kelvin, always kg/mol. KE per molecule = 3kT/2, per mole = 3RT/2.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: NEB 2023 (5): kinetic theory + its assumptions. NEB 2022 (3): rms speed of O₂ at 27 °C. NEB 2022 (4): gas at 27 °C, 10⁵ Pa, 0.5 m³ → volume at 100 °C constant pressure.
